page: Amazon Web Services m9g.medium is a general-purpose instance powered by a single-core AWS Graviton processor. Built on the ARMv9 architecture with Neoverse-V3 cores, this instance features 1 dedicated vCPU operating at 3.3 GHz, 1 physical core, and 1 thread per core. The processor includes 64 KB of L1d cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 48 MB of L3 cache. It is equipped with 4.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. The instance runs on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, lacks local storage, has no GPU, and offers a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps.

Benchmark data reveals a clear contrast between single-threaded and multi-threaded performance. Due to its single vCPU configuration, multi-core stress-ng performance is limited, matching its single-core score of 1988.18. However, single-threaded operations show strong capabilities, with gzip compression achieving 36.08 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression reaching 17.04 GB/sec, both placing in the top tier. Conversely, memory bandwidth is mixed; while large-block read-only bandwidth is average at 43.27 GB/sec, small-block cached reads and large-block writes are relatively low. Passmark CPU and database operation scores are weak to poor, and Redis SET operations perform at 3.25 million operations per second.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the m9g.medium offers a low-entry hardware profile utilizing AWS's custom ARM architecture, which typically provides high resource density for lightweight workloads. The lack of bundled local storage and public IPv4 addresses highlights its role as a basic node in a larger, network-attached storage architecture. It is best suited for lightweight general-purpose workloads, single-threaded utility scripts, basic web serving, and small-scale development or testing environments that do not require multi-threaded parallel processing.
